phase3_findings.description: Latent fail-open: classify() first-match ordering returns pending_count=0 for a provenance file that ALSO matches an earlier frozen bucket (record/historical/tooling/transient). scan() independently recovers the frozen-provenance VALUE count (protecting the reverse stale-provenance guard) but does NOT independently recover the pending REMAINDER, so renameable prose in such a file would escape the forward AC3 guard. Not exploitable in the current tree — the four declared provenance files sit under none of the earlier prefixes — so no live RED is missed; latent only if a future provenance entry names a file under one of those prefixes.

Test-hardening gap (analyzer labeled Important/sev5, capped to Minor: it is a missing edge-case test on a lint that is itself test infrastructure, not a shipped-code defect). The scan() frozen-provenance first-match-independence recount (lines 202-206) is UNTESTED: no fixture provenance file also matches an earlier frozen bucket, so deleting the independent recount and reusing classify()'s fcount would still pass every assertion. Recommend a fixture provenance file also under record_prefixes/tooling_files carrying a quoted "DevFlow" value.

Test-hardening gap (analyzer labeled Important/sev5, capped to Minor). --update-baseline mutation (add a newly-appeared pending file / drop a swept row) is UNTESTED; only the idempotent already-reconciled case (same 3 files) is exercised. The reseed's actual drain/add job is never asserted. Relevant because the deferred sweep follow-up drives the drain via --update-baseline.

Reverse-stale detection covers only provenance and pending_sweep_baseline, not record_prefixes/historical_files/tooling_files/transient lists — those config lists can rot (deleted/no-longer-matching file) undetected. Consistent with the docstring's stated scope; fail direction is toward over-freezing (only suppresses, cannot introduce a false clean for a new occurrence elsewhere), so it does not defeat AC3. Recorded as a known decision.

--update-baseline and --print-population pass no `skipped` list to iter_blobs, so an unreadable tracked file is breadcrumbed but silently omitted from a reseed. Mitigated because reconcile mode still fails closed on the same file. A shared skipped-handling would remove the asymmetry; matters for the deferred sweep's reseed step.

A few clean-run negative assertions (learnings/x.jsonl absent, fake-tool.py absent) test a substring's absence from output that contains no findings lines at all, so they pass trivially and carry weight only alongside the rc=0 assertion. Not harmful; not independent routing proofs. The transient-exception firing is proven only indirectly via rc=0 — a direct --print-population assertion would be stronger.

Presence-based reconciliation means an already-pending high-churn file (run.sh, CLAUDE.md, baselined) silently accepts unlimited new brand-cased DevFlow. Documented intended churn/concurrency-safety tradeoff; the deferred sweep drains the baseline. Noted so the drain follow-up does not blindly rename frozen references inside mixed files.

Cosmetic: lint prints `audited {audited} of {audited} files` — same variable twice, so `of N` conveys nothing (readable count and total are never distinguished; skipped files are still counted in audited). Real-tree test greps `audited (\d+) of`, so harmless but slightly misleading.

report: Independent blinded shadow pass over PR #1973 (issue #1745 enforcement mechanism only; AC2 prose sweep deferred). Full Phase 0-4.3 fan-out: code-reviewer, silent-failure-hunter, comment-analyzer, pr-test-analyzer, and the final-pass requesting-code-review all dispatched and returned; type-design-analyzer gated out (no new types). Verified independently: real tree exits 0 (1120 files audited), ruff clean, 163 pending baseline files (all high-churn hot-spots grandfathered so presence-based reconciliation is concurrent-merge safe). No Critical or genuinely blocking Important finding: the two items pr-test-analyzer labeled Important are missing edge-case tests on the lint's own test block (untested frozen-provenance independence recount; untested --update-baseline mutation) rather than shipped-code defects, and are capped to Minor. The one latent fail-open (silent-failure-hunter) is non-exploitable in the current tree and latent only under a future provenance-file/frozen-bucket collision. Remaining findings are Suggestions (cosmetic status line, documented presence-not-count tradeoff, reverse-stale scope, reseed asymmetry). Verdict: APPROVE, with the two untested-branch gaps recommended as low-cost test hardening (non-blocking).
